newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan paper shares up on hopes of pulp price hike.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan paper shares up on hopes of pulp price hike.

text.p: Shares in Taiwan's paper sector surged in early Thursday trading on expected pulp price rises in the second quarter, brokers said.
After 45 minutes, the paper sector soared 3.74 percent while the overall index rose 1.3 percent.
Taiwan Pulp rose the daily seven percent limit to T$34, and Yuen Foong Yu was up T$1.3 or 4.53 percent to T$30.
"Following recent international pulp price rises, the local pulp price is expected to rise in the second quarter," said Nikko Securities research chief Leonard Hsueh.

Hsueh said share prices also would rise in the sector on rising demand for paper. "This round of pulp and paper price hikes should be pretty solid and healthy as they will be driven by actual demand," he said.

Hsueh said Yuen Foong Yu's rise in part reflected an expected rise in its non-operating earnings, as two of its subsidiaries plan to apply for listing in the fledgling over-the-counter stock market in May or June.
The planned listings would enhance profits of the parent company, brokers said.
